therapy_note: Khamaj is the raag of lightness — it is the most commonly used raag in thumri (the light-classical romantic form), dadra, and hori (festival songs). Unlike the serious major raags, Khamaj does not ask you to go deep inward. It invites you to be present, easy, and joyful. The use of both komal and shuddh Ni gives it a flexible, playful quality — it can shift between tender and bright in the same breath.

classical_reference: Girija Devi and Shobha Gurtu are the definitive Khamaj interpreters. It is the thaat (parent scale) for multiple raags. Bandish: 'Kaun Gali Gayo Shyam'
notes_for_vocalist: Khamaj has a unique feature — both komal Ni and shuddh Ni can be used, giving the performer freedom. In thumri style, this flexibility is exploited beautifully. Pa is sometimes skipped in ascent. This raag demands a relaxed, liquid vocal style — stiffness kills Khamaj. It is the raag most associated with thumri ang (romantic style) and should be approached with playfulness.
